tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill whenever...'), lists explicit trigger contexts (named target group with unhealthy targets, specific reason codes like Target.Timeout, 5xx with no healthy targets, UnHealthyHostCount alarm), covers multiple target types, and explicitly excludes out-of-scope cases (Classic LB, Gateway LB). It is a few sentences long and concise given the complexity of the trigger conditions it needs to disambiguate.
tests.evidence: Diagnose unhealthy targets in an Application Load Balancer (ALB) or Network Load Balancer (NLB) target group. Use this skill whenever a prompt names an ALB/NLB target group and says targets are unhealthy, health checks are failing, a target-health reason code such as Target.Timeout appears, or the load balancer returns 5xx/503 with no healthy targets.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body jumps straight into domain-specific procedures (reason codes, SG/NACL interplay, target-type branching) without explaining general concepts like what an ALB is or how health checks generally work. Each section conveys non-obvious, project-specific facts.
tests.evidence: **ALB fail-open.** If every target in the group is unhealthy, the ALB routes to all of them anyway.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Large lookup tables (cause-class mapping, resource exhaustion metrics) are correctly deferred to references/decision-tree.md and only loaded conditionally at Steps 5 and 6, rather than embedded inline in the body.
tests.evidence: Load the metric list in [references/decision-tree.md](references/decision-tree.md#resource-exhaustion-metrics-step-5) only when you reach this step.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The single reference file decision-tree.md is linked twice via markdown links with anchors.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Both links specify precisely when to load the file — only at Step 5 for resource exhaustion metrics and Step 6 for the cause-class mapping table.
tests.evidence: Load the metric list in [references/decision-tree.md](references/decision-tree.md#resource-exhaustion-metrics-step-5) only when you reach this step.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths from the skill root with no traversal or absolute paths.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: The skill is highly prescriptive for the fragile diagnostic decision tree (exact order, exact reason-code routing) while leaving flexibility for reporting format and permission handling, matching prescriptiveness to fragility well.
tests.evidence: `Target.ResponseCodeMismatch` -> app returns a code outside the matcher on the HC path -> `HEALTH_CHECK_CONFIG` (path/matcher). Go to Step 6.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: No menu of equal alternative tools is presented; the skill specifies exact AWS API calls to use for each situation without offering competing options.
tests.evidence: Run these calls yourself in this conversation (for example with `use_aws`).

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The workflow teaches a generalizable diagnostic procedure (branch on target type, route by reason code, validate, report) applicable to any ALB/NLB unhealthy-target scenario, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: Step 2: Branch on target type (instance | ip | lambda | ecs-awsvpc).

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: A dedicated Gotchas section lists concrete, non-obvious environment-specific facts (Lambda has no target-side SG, NACLs stateless, no grace period on target groups, etc.).
tests.evidence: **NACLs are stateless.** A missing ephemeral-port return rule looks like a timeout with clean security groups.

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: Step 8 defines what to report (cause class, affected targets, evidence, corrected setting) and the cause-class-to-fix mapping lives in the reference table; this is sufficient structured guidance without needing a separate large template file.
tests.evidence: Step 8: Report the cause class, affected targets, evidence, and the corrected setting for the operator to apply via IaC.

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline output template exists in the body; the output structure is described briefly in Step 8 without a verbose skeleton.
tests.evidence: Step 8: Report the cause class, affected targets, evidence, and the corrected setting for the operator to apply via IaC. Never apply it.
